notes: Topic: boron-nitride-filled silicone films for flexible thermal interfaces. Question: whether platelet orientation improves through-plane thermal transport without a major loss of compliance. Approach: compare vertically oriented and randomly dispersed platelets at the same 20 vol% filler fraction; same silicone formulation and cure. Through-plane thermal conductivity at 25 °C: aligned 1.8 ± 0.2 W m−1 K−1; random 0.9 ± 0.1 W m−1 K−1; mean ± sample SD, five independently prepared films per group. Tensile modulus at 25 °C: aligned 2.4 ± 0.3 MPa, random 2.2 ± 0.2 MPa; same n and SD definition. After 500 bending cycles at 5 mm radius, the aligned films retained 92% of their initial thermal conductivity. No statistical hypothesis tests were performed. Orientation was assessed by cross-sectional microscopy; interfacial thermal resistance was not measured. No device-level temperature measurements. Contribution: an orientation-based processing route that improved the measured through-plane conductivity in this formulation. Scope: this filler fraction and testing conditions; mechanism of the improvement not isolated.

anonymous_outputs.A: Platelet orientation offers a processing variable for balancing thermal transport and compliance in boron-nitride-filled silicone films for flexible thermal interfaces. We compared vertically oriented and randomly dispersed platelets at 20 vol% using the same silicone formulation and cure, with orientation assessed by cross-sectional microscopy. At 25 °C, through-plane thermal conductivity was 1.8 ± 0.2 W m−1 K−1 for aligned films and 0.9 ± 0.1 W m−1 K−1 for randomly filled films. The corresponding tensile moduli were 2.4 ± 0.3 and 2.2 ± 0.2 MPa. Values are means ± sample standard deviations from five independently prepared films per group; no statistical hypothesis tests were performed. Aligned films retained 92% of their initial thermal conductivity after 500 bending cycles at a 5 mm radius. Thus, alignment doubled the mean measured conductivity while producing a comparatively small increase in mean modulus. This processing route improved through-plane transport within the tested formulation and conditions, although the mechanism was not isolated: interfacial thermal resistance was not measured, and device-level temperature reduction remains untested.

Here, we examined whether vertical alignment of boron nitride platelets increases through-plane thermal conductivity in silicone films without a major loss of compliance. Vertically oriented and randomly dispersed films were prepared at the same filler fraction of 20 vol% using identical silicone formulations and curing conditions. Cross-sectional microscopy was used to assess orientation. At 25 °C, through-plane thermal conductivity was 1.8 ± 0.2 W m−1 K−1 for aligned films and 0.9 ± 0.1 W m−1 K−1 for random films, whereas tensile moduli were 2.4 ± 0.3 and 2.2 ± 0.2 MPa, respectively. Values are means ± sample standard deviations from five independently prepared films per group; no hypothesis tests were performed. Aligned films retained 92% of their initial conductivity after 500 bending cycles at a 5 mm radius. These results support improved measured conductivity with a modest increase in mean modulus under the tested conditions. Interfacial resistance, the underlying mechanism, and device-level thermal performance remain unresolved.

notes: System: a disulfide-containing polyester network. Compare thermal treatments at 110 °C for 15 and 60 min. Sol fraction after THF extraction increased from 8% to 19%; storage modulus at 1 Hz and 25 °C decreased from 6.0 to 3.8 MPa. Mean of three separately prepared specimens per condition; no error estimates or statistical tests supplied. DSC Tg was approximately 42 °C for both conditions, within the measurement resolution. FTIR showed no resolvable change in ester carbonyl position. SEC of the soluble fraction showed a broader low-molar-mass shoulder after 60 min, using polystyrene calibration. The insoluble network was not analyzed by SEC. An ester-only control without disulfides was not available. Possible interpretations: network rearrangement and/or chain scission during prolonged heating; not uniquely distinguished. Constant carbonyl position does not exclude low levels of ester cleavage. Applications in reprocessing are a motivation, but reprocessing cycles, recyclability and long-term creep were not tested. Next discriminating step: compare an otherwise matched ester-only network and perform end-group analysis; this is proposed future work, not completed.

anonymous_outputs.A: Prolonged heating at 110 °C altered the extractability and mechanical response of the disulfide-containing polyester network. Increasing the treatment duration from 15 to 60 min raised the THF sol fraction from 8% to 19% and lowered the storage modulus at 1 Hz and 25 °C from 6.0 to 3.8 MPa. These changes are consistent with network rearrangement and/or chain scission, but do not uniquely identify either process. The reported values are means from three separately prepared specimens per condition; without error estimates or statistical tests, their variability cannot be assessed. The approximately unchanged DSC glass-transition temperature of 42 °C indicates no resolved shift under these measurement conditions. Likewise, the absence of a resolvable shift in the ester carbonyl band does not exclude low levels of ester cleavage. The broader low-molar-mass shoulder observed by SEC after 60 min provides additional evidence of changes in the soluble material, although polystyrene calibration and exclusion of the insoluble network limit its interpretation. Attribution to disulfide chemistry also remains uncertain without an ester-only control. An otherwise matched ester-only network and end-group analysis would help distinguish the proposed processes. Although these observations motivate reprocessing studies, they do not establish recyclability, performance over repeated reprocessing cycles, or resistance to long-term creep.
